## Position
Formentera has no airport. The only way in is the ferry from Ibiza, and every
ferry docks at the port of La Savina. The hostal is on the first line of that
port, roughly 200 m — two to three minutes on foot — from the ferry terminal.

Approximate road distances: Sant Francesc Xavier (capital) 3 km · Ses Illetes
beach 5 km · Es Pujols 6 km · La Mola lighthouse 22 km.

## Restaurant
Welcoming and family-run, in the same building as the hostal, with a large terrace overlooking the port.
You can enjoy all kinds of dishes here, as well as our specialities: lobster and crab stew, grilled fish platters and fish zarzuela, seafood and meat paellas, and fisherman's-style rice.

Menu (indicative — no prices are published):
- Rice dishes & paellas: Fish paella, Mixed paella, Seafood paella, Paella Bellavista, Arroz a la marinera, Arroz a banda, Fideuà
- From the sea: Lobster stew, Crab stew, Fish zarzuela, Grilled fish platter, Fresh island fish, oven-baked, Fresh fish baked in salt, Seafood platter
- From the grill: Mixed grilled meats, Selection of chargrilled meats

Opening hours: NOT PUBLISHED. Menu prices: NOT PUBLISHED.

## Services
- Vehicle hire: Cars, motorbikes, scooters and bicycles to explore the island, straight from the hostal door.
- Bar and terrace: A large terrace facing the moorings — for breakfast, lunch, or a drink as the sun goes down.
- Beside the ferry: A few metres from the quay where the boats from Ibiza arrive: no taxis, no transfers when you land.
- Local advice: We will tell you which coves to visit, when the markets are on and where to catch the best sunset.

## The island, from the property
- La Savina (0 km): The port and the gateway to Formentera: the Ibiza ferries dock here, and so do we. A constant coming and going of fishing boats, sailing yachts and pleasure craft, with the promenade right outside the door.
- Sant Francesc Xavier (3 km): The island's capital, three kilometres from the port. Its square holds the town hall and the 18th-century church, once used as a fortress against Barbary raids. The best place for shopping and for the craft market.
- Sant Ferran (5 km): The village you pass through on the way to La Mola and Es Pujols, with a good spread of bars and restaurants. A fine place to eat slowly or have a drink and watch the world go by.
- Es Pujols (6 km): The most touristic village and the liveliest after dark, with shops, restaurants, bars and late-night places. The beach has fine sand and shallow water.
- La Mola (22 km): The highest and most distant point of the island, with its lighthouse on the cliff edge and the hippy market on Wednesdays and Sundays. The road up is one of the most beautiful on Formentera.
- Ses Illetes (5 km): Inside the Ses Salines Natural Park and minutes from the hostal: white sand and turquoise water that stands comparison with any Caribbean beach. Busy in August, almost empty out of season.

## Frequently asked
Q: How do I get to the hostal?
A: Formentera has no airport: you arrive by ferry from Ibiza, and every ferry docks at the port of La Savina. The hostal is on the first line of that same port, so you will see us as you step off the boat. No taxi or transfer needed.

Q: How far is it from the ferry?
A: About 200 metres — two or three minutes on foot with a suitcase. It is why many guests choose us for the first and last night of a trip.

Q: Is there WiFi in the rooms?
A: Yes. Every room has free WiFi, and there is coverage in the hostal's common areas too.

Q: Do the rooms have air conditioning?
A: Yes, every room has air conditioning, along with a private bathroom, television, desk and wardrobe.

Q: Does the hostal have a restaurant?
A: Yes, in the same building, with a large terrace overlooking the port. It serves Mediterranean cooking and seafood: lobster stew, rice dishes and paellas, fresh island fish and chargrilled meats. It is open to non-residents as well.

Q: Can I hire a car or a scooter?
A: Yes. We arrange car, motorbike, scooter and bicycle hire from the hostal itself, so you do not have to go anywhere to collect it. It is much the easiest way to see the island.

Q: What languages does reception speak?
A: Spanish, Catalan, English and Italian.

Q: How many people fit in a room?
A: The hostal's rooms sleep two. If there are more of you, ask us: we have 38 rooms, plus three apartments on the island sleeping three, four and five.

Q: Are the apartments in the hostal?
A: No. Can Loca (Es Pujols), Can Peix 22 (La Savina) and Barbaroja (Ca Marí) are separate, self-catering properties elsewhere on the island, with their own kitchen and no restaurant or reception service. You will want a vehicle if you stay in one.

Q: When is the best time to visit?
A: July and August have the most going on, but they are also the busiest. May, June, September and October are usually the sweet spot: the sea is still warm, the light is clearer and the island is far quieter. Between November and April the average is around 16°C.

Q: Is it worth booking direct?
A: Yes. Booking through this site gets you the best available rate with no intermediary commission, and you deal directly with us if anything needs changing.
